questions.prompt: Complete the third conditional: "If she ___ harder, she would have passed."

options.text: studied
would have studied
has studied
had studied

questions.explanation: The third conditional uses 'if + past perfect' in the if-clause: 'had studied'. "studied" uses past simple, which is correct for the second conditional (unreal present), not the third. "has studied" uses present perfect, which has no place in a conditional if-clause. "would have studied" uses 'would have', which belongs in the result clause, never in the if-clause.

questions.prompt: Complete the wish: "I wish I ___ the answer." (The speaker doesn't know the answer right now.)

options.text: know
have known
knew
had known

questions.explanation: For a present wish about something untrue now, use 'wish + past simple': 'I wish I knew'. "know" keeps the present tense — 'I wish I know' is grammatically wrong. "have known" uses present perfect, which is not standard after 'wish' for a present state. "had known" uses past perfect, which would express a past regret ('I wish I had known'), not a present wish.

questions.prompt: "Unless you hurry, you'll be late." This means the same as:

options.text: If you hurry, you'll be late.
If you hurry, you won't be late.
Unless you don't hurry, you'll be late.
If you don't hurry, you'll be late.

questions.explanation: 'Unless' means 'if … not', so 'Unless you hurry' = 'If you don't hurry, you'll be late'. "If you hurry, you'll be late" reverses the condition — 'if you hurry' would mean being on time. "Unless" doubles the negative ('unless … don't'), which is incorrect. "If you hurry, you won't be late" changes both the condition and the result.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is a MIXED conditional (past condition, present result)?

options.text: If she had studied harder, she would have passed.
If I had taken that job, I would be rich now.
If I weren't so tired, I would have gone yesterday.
If it rains, I will stay in.

questions.explanation: "taken that job" is Mixed A: past condition (if + past perfect 'had taken') → present result (would + base 'would be… now'). "studied harder, she" is a pure third conditional (past → past). "weren't so tired" is Mixed B: present condition (if + past simple 'weren't') → past result (would + have + pp 'would have gone'). "If it rains, I will stay in" is a first conditional (real future).

options.text: I wish I had arrived earlier.
I wish he would stop making that noise.
I wish I went to the concert last night.
I wish I were taller.

questions.explanation: "I wish I went to the concert last night" is wrong: past simple after 'wish' expresses a present wish about something untrue now, not a past regret. To express regret about last night, you need past perfect: 'I wish I had gone to the concert last night'. "I wish I had arrived earlier" correctly uses past perfect for a past regret. "I wish he would stop making that noise" correctly uses 'would' for an annoyance directed at someone else. "I wish I were taller" correctly uses past simple ('were') for a present wish.
